function.name: generate_report
function.description: Generates a comprehensive report based on user activity data within a specified time frame. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_id.description: The unique identifier for the user.

start_date.description: The start date for the report period in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

end_date.description: The end date for the report period, inclusive, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

include_inactive.description: Flag to determine if inactive users should be included in the report.

report_format.description: The format in which the report will be generated.

message.content:
**Ionisation – A Quick Guide** | Method | Principle | Typical Energy / Conditions | Strengths | Weaknesses | Common Applications | |--------|-----------|-----------------------------|----------|------------|---------------------| | **Electron Impact (EI)** | Fast electrons collide with molecules → knock out an electron → cation + secondary fragments | ~70 eV electrons, high vacuum | *Hard* fragmentation gives rich structural info; reproducible & fast | Requires gas‑phase analytes; not suitable for thermally labile compounds | Gas chromatography–mass spec (GC‑MS) | | **Chemical Ionisation (CI)** | Reagent gas (CH₄, NH₃…) reacts with primary EI ions → proton transfer or adduct formation | Low energy (~10 eV); same GC column | *Soft* ionisation preserves molecular ion; good for polar organics | Lower sensitivity than EI; requires compatible reagents | GC‑MS when intact M⁺ desired | | **ElectroSpray Ionisation (ESI)** | Charged droplets formed at capillary tip → solvent evaporates → charged analyte ions remain | Ambient pressure, low voltage (<5 kV) | Very soft; works directly from solution; handles large biomolecules | Suppression effects (matrix, salts); limited to polar species | LC‑MS/MS, proteomics, metabolomics | | **Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionisation (MALDI)** | Sample mixed with matrix absorbs laser pulse → desorbs/ionsize analyte | UV/NIR lasers (337 nm, 355 nm, 532 nm) | Handles very large proteins/polymers; minimal fragmentation | Needs crystalline matrix prep; less quantitative | Protein fingerprinting, peptide sequencing | | **Atmospheric Pressure Chemical Ionisation (APCI)** | Corona discharge produces reagent ions → charge transfer to analyte | Similar to ESI but uses corona needle | Good for moderately nonpolar small molecules; tolerant to solvents | Less efficient for highly polar analytes | LC‑MS of pharmaceuticals, lipids | | **Photoionisation (PI)** | Photons (UV/X‑ray) eject electrons from analyte | Tunable photon energies (20–100 eV) | Soft, tunable; no reagent gases | Limited to transparent samples; lower cross sections | Atmospheric chemistry studies, trace gas detection | | **Laser Ablation Ionisation (LAI)** | High‑power pulsed laser vaporises solid sample → plasma forms ions | Nanosecond pulses, >1 MW/cm² | Direct sampling of solids; rapid | Plasma background complicates spectra | Geochemical analyses, forensic science | --- ### How to Pick “the Best” Method? | Decision Factor | Recommended Choice | |-----------------|--------------------| | **Sample state** (solid/liquid/gas) | Solid → MALDI/Laser ablation
Liquid → ESI/APCI
Gas → EI/CI | | **Desired ion type** (molecular vs fragment) | Want intact molecule → CI, ESI, APCI, PI
Want detailed structure → EI | | **Mass range** | <500 Da → EI, CI, APCI
Large biomolecules (>2000 Da) → ESI, MALDI | | **Sensitivity needs** | Highest sensitivity often achieved with ESI/APCI (especially tandem MS). | | **Complexity of matrix** | Polar matrices → ESI may suffer suppression; consider cleanup or use APCI. | | **Instrumentation constraints** | If you only have a GC system → EI/CI.
If you have LC-MS → ESI/APCI. | | **Speed** | Rapid screening → EI (fast injection)
Detailed profiling → ESI/Tandem MS | --- #### Practical Tips 1. **Use Tandem Mass Spectrometry (MS/MS)** whenever possible—regardless of ionisation source—to confirm identity via characteristic product ions. 2. **Optimize Source Parameters:** For ESI, adjust spray voltage, flow rate, nebulizer gas, and drying temperature to reduce salt/adduct peaks. 3. **Consider Hybrid Sources:** Some instruments combine APPI (atmospheric pressure photoionisation) with ESI for complementary coverage. 4. **Check Compatibility:** Certain analytes degrade under harsh conditions (high temp, strong electric fields). Use softer sources (CE, MALDI). --- ### Bottom Line There isn’t a single “best” ionisation technique—it depends entirely on your analytical goals: - **For routine organic compound identification in GC‑MS:** Electron Impact (hard, reliable). - **When preserving the parent ion matters (metabolites, drugs):** Chemical Ionisation or Photoionisation. - **For complex biological mixtures (proteins, peptides):** Electrospray or MALDI. - **If you’re analyzing atmospheric trace gases:** Photoionisation or Resonance Enhanced Multi‑Photon Ionisation (REMPI). Choose the one whose strengths align most closely with your sample characteristics, required resolution, and available instrumentation.
